maria: FYI seeing a P99 bump on the autotune rollout — short-seq requests (<=64) went from ~1.9s -> ~2.2s after kernel path changes. suspect rapid kernel handoffs during continuous-batching window.
jonathan: which model/hardware + cbatch config?
maria: mistral-7b @ H100-80GB, cbatch_window=30ms, sticky_kernel_ttl=0 (we disabled sticky in autotune). profiler shows kernel_switch events every ~1–3 requests.
evan: can you paste the profiler snippet?
maria: paste:
```
[profiler] req_id=... kernel_switch_ms=6.8 launch_overhead_ms=3.2 kv_miss=true
[metrics] recent_p99=2200ms avg_latency=320ms kernel_switches_per_min=18
```
akshay: this matches theory — disabling sticky makes the scheduler aggressively move between architecture-aware kernels as seqlen varies in cbatch. each switch pays launch+warmup. try sticky_kernel_ttl=150-250ms.
evan: quick microbench on canary:
- sticky=0: p99=2200ms, mean=320ms
- sticky=200ms: p99=1980ms, mean=304ms
cost: cpu for scheduler ~+3%
so p99 down ~10%.
akshay: caveat — long-seq throughput can suffer if sticky holds a suboptimal kernel. propose sequence-aware sticky rule instead of global TTL. config draft:
```
kernel_autotune:
  sticky_ttl_ms: 200
  sticky_condition: "recent_p90_seq <= kernel_pref_seqlen * 1.25"
```
maria: ran A/B on 5% traffic for 1h with that heuristic: p99 back to baseline (1.92s), kernel_switches_per_min -> 3, long-seq throughput neutral.
perf-bot: deploy/metric-check ok for the canary (no error spike)
ops-bot: schedule progressive rollout + 30m watch. if p99 > 2.1s revert.
jonathan: nice. can we add small hysteresis on the condition so transient spikes don't flip kernel? maybe require 3/5 windows.
akshay: yes — we'll implement sticky_count_threshold=3. we'll push a patch to autotune and run larger canary tomorrow.
maria: thanks — filing incident note and will attach profiler traces.
(evans and akshay react :thumbsup:)
